aiOverview.content: Álvaro Uribe Vélez (born July 4, 1952) is a highly polarizing former president of Colombia who served from 2002 to 2010. His presidency was marked by a strict security policy against guerillas, yet he has faced long-standing legal battles regarding witness tampering and ties to paramilitary groups, with a 2025 conviction overturned on appeal,The Guardian reported. Key Aspects of Álvaro Uribe Vélez: Terms in Office: Served two terms (2002–2010) and is credited with improving national security against the FARC guerrilla group Freedom.fiu.edu reports. Legal Challenges: In August 2025, Uribe was sentenced to 12 years of house arrest for bribery and witness tampering, as discussed in this YouTube video and detailed in this PBS news article. However, this conviction was overturned by an appeals court in October 2025 due to "structural deficiencies" in the case, according to this YouTube video and The Guardian. Political Legacy: While admired by supporters as a transformative leader, he is heavily criticized by opponents for human rights violations allegedly committed by right-wing paramilitaries during his time in office, according to this YouTube video and the National Security Archive. Note: As of August 2025, a separate political figure, Senator Miguel Uribe, was reported to have died following a shooting, distinct from the former president, as reported by this YouTube video and the BBC.
